dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a parity test (or single-source the probe module) ensuring `_capabilities` capability probes match `_optional.EXTRAS` probes for overlapping extras.
evidence: src/rebar/_optional.py:35 `EXTRAS: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {` with probes e.g. `"agents": ("pydantic_ai", ...)`, `"metrics": ("lizard", ...)`
src/rebar/_capabilities.py CAPABILITIES entries duplicate the same probe strings, e.g. `probe="pydantic_ai"`, `probe="lizard"`

tests/unit/test_capabilities.py asserts pyproject-extra parity and internal validate() cleanliness but contains no assertion cross-checking `_capabilities` probe modules against `_optional.EXTRAS` probes — ABSENCE of a drift guard.
dropped.finding: Two parallel probe registries now coexist — the historical `_optional.EXTRAS` (extra -> probe module) and the new `_capabilities.CAPABILITIES` (key -> probe module) — with overlapping extras (agents/pydantic_ai, grounding/tree_sitter_language_pack, metrics/lizard, wiki/pypandoc, adf/marklas, s3/git_remote_s3, tracing/opentelemetry). The probe module names must stay identical across both, but no test asserts parity between the two probe sets, so they can silently drift (e.g. one updated when a probe module is renamed, the other not), yielding inconsistent availability detection.
scenarios: A probe module import name changes and only one of the two registries is updated, causing capability_installed / extra_installed to disagree.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Document at `Route.capabilities` that advertised values are now semantic capability keys (not packaging extras), noting the spelling change.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py:645-649 `_check_capabilities` yields `unknown_capability` for any route capability not in KNOWN_CAPABILITIES
search of `_registry.py` for `capabilities=(` returned no matches — no route currently advertises a capability, so no live break.
dropped.finding: KNOWN_CAPABILITIES changed identity from packaging-extra spellings ({'mcp','reviewbot','ui','agents'}) to semantic capability keys (CAPABILITY_KEYS, e.g. 'mcp_server','review_bot','audit_ui','agent_runtime'). Any Route that advertised a capability using the old extra-name spelling would now fail _check_capabilities validation with 'unknown_capability'. No current route in ROUTES sets `capabilities=` (all default to ()), so nothing breaks today, but the contract for the `Route.capabilities` field has silently changed from extra-names to semantic-keys with no migration note at the field definition.
scenarios: A future or downstream route advertising the old extra-name (e.g. capabilities=('ui',)) now fails validation and must use 'audit_ui' instead.
